name: Chen Lanjie
current_role: Listed as a founder of Advance Intelligence Group (Singapore); possibly Group CEO 'Jefferson Chen' (unconfirmed)
profile: Advance Intelligence Group, founded in Singapore in 2016, grew from an AI/identity-verification SaaS provider (ADVANCE.AI) into a Southeast Asian digital-finance group with Indonesian lender Kredit Pintar and BNPL app Atome. Backers include SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Warburg Pincus and Northstar. Group CEO Jefferson Chen is named by investors as the leader, but it is unconfirmed whether he is 'Chen Lanjie'.
interesting_fact: Investors say the group went from a SaaS analytics provider to Indonesia's top digital lending platform within a few years of its 2016 founding; it was ranked No. 5 in 'Singapore Top Startups 2023'.
notes: Identity not confirmed: could not verify that 'Chen Lanjie' is the romanised Chinese name of CEO Jefferson Chen (the ADVANCE.AI site also lists Dong Shou as co-founder). Web-search budget ran out mid-lane; re-check before outreach. No published press email found.

name: Brad Fitzpatrick
profile: American programmer (b. 1980) who created LiveJournal as a college freshman and sold it via Danga Interactive to Six Apart in 2005, along the way writing memcached, OpenID, Gearman and MogileFS. At Google (2007-2020) he worked on Android performance (StrictMode) and the Go language team, then joined Tailscale in Jan 2020 as a late-stage co-founder.
interesting_fact: LiveJournal grew out of a journaling program he wrote for himself as an 18-year-old college freshman; it became a company (Danga Interactive) that he sold to Six Apart in January 2005.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Beaverton, Oregon (Aloha High School) and started his first company, FreeVote.com, while still in high school. He also built Android's StrictMode API, and his long-running side obsession Perkeep (formerly Camlistore) is what pulled him onto Google's Go team full-time.

public_contacts.value: https://www.linkedin.com/in/bradfitz (he notes it is mostly unused)

notes: Self-published email on bradfitz.com. A legendary engineer with web-scale infrastructure credentials (memcached, written for LiveJournal), which makes for a strong podcast angle. Active on X and GitHub.
